subject.title: Add structured process events for sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class session process-event contract now, and if so what taxonomy, replay/retention model, and authorization boundary should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent event taxonomy and security boundary are public core API decisions that automation should not choose.

options.title: Design core process events
options.body: Approve a single additive gateway/session contract covering taxonomy, replay, ordering, redaction, and client mappings before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to existing progress issues
options.body: Keep this as design context and implement only narrower surfaces such as sessions_send progress or CLI stdout streaming in their own canonical issues.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Leave current item/tool/lifecycle streams as the only supported progress surfaces until stronger product demand or a missing API blocker appears.

recommendation.title: Design core process events
recommendation.body: Approve a single additive gateway/session contract covering taxonomy, replay, ordering, redaction, and client mappings before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is repeated ownership of gateway event catalogs, session progress behavior, and related protocol docs.
